research_mode: official MHCLG and GOV.UK Residential PEEPs guidance only; review, Fire and Rescue Authority information-sharing and secure-information methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Timely mitigation implementation
verified_claims: Measures assessed as reasonable and proportionate should be implemented in a reasonably timely manner.
limitations: The guidance does not specify one universal completion deadline.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Compartmentation mitigation guard
verified_claims: An in-flat measure that compromises building compartmentation is described as extremely unlikely to be reasonable and proportionate.
limitations: Each proposed measure still requires technical and case-specific assessment.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Common-area and service-charge impact
verified_claims: Measures adversely affecting common-area users or causing excessive service-charge increases are described as extremely unlikely to be reasonable and proportionate.
limitations: Impact and legal rights require case-by-case analysis.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Paid evacuation-staff guard
verified_claims: Employing paid staff primarily to support evacuation under Residential PEEPs, such as a waking-watch arrangement, is described as extremely unlikely to be reasonable and proportionate.
limitations: This statement does not determine duties under separate temporary-risk or enforcement arrangements.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Emergency evacuation statement format
verified_claims: There is no prescribed statement format beyond being written; the guidance recommends a short clear record of the resident's agreed action.
limitations: A short format must still contain enough building- and resident-specific information.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Resident consent and withdrawal
verified_claims: Resident consent is required for the PCFRA and information sharing, and the resident may withdraw consent at any time.
limitations: Withdrawal must be recorded and acted upon lawfully without erasing other statutory records improperly.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: PCFRA outcome and decision records
verified_claims: The guidance recommends recording PCFRA outcomes, mitigation decision-making and cases where no evacuation statement was agreed.
limitations: A complete record does not prove that decisions were reasonable or measures effective.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Annual Residential PEEPs review
verified_claims: The PCFRA, mitigations and evacuation statement must be reviewed within 12 months and within each 12-month period thereafter.
limitations: Review scheduling does not establish that changes were implemented.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Change- and resident-request review triggers
verified_claims: Review is also required where amendment may be needed or at a relevant resident's reasonable request, including changed condition or material building change.
limitations: A request or change does not predetermine the review outcome.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Post-drill and incident review
verified_claims: The guidance recommends reviewing the process after planned drills or emergency incidents, especially where mitigations did not operate as expected.
limitations: A drill does not replicate every real-fire condition or resident circumstance.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Prescribed Fire and Rescue Authority information
verified_claims: With explicit resident agreement, the responsible person must share flat number, floor number, indicative assistance level and whether an evacuation statement exists.
limitations: The prescribed fields do not include a full medical or care record.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Information for all participating relevant residents
verified_claims: Information sharing applies to relevant residents who engage even where they have volunteer or other evacuation support arrangements.
limitations: Sharing remains conditional on explicit resident agreement.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Concise operational resident information
verified_claims: Resident information made available to the Fire and Rescue Authority should be limited, accessible and concise enough to support an emergency operational response.
limitations: Conciseness must not omit prescribed fields or create ambiguous assistance categories.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Data protection and secure information box
verified_claims: Information sharing must comply with data-protection law, and where a secure information box is used it must meet the applicable Fire Safety (England) Regulations requirements.
limitations: A secure box does not itself demonstrate lawful access control or current contents.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Additional Fire and Rescue Authority information requests
verified_claims: A Fire and Rescue Authority may request additional digital information with resident consent, but the responsible person has no legal duty under these Regulations to share more than the prescribed information.
limitations: Other legal duties or emergency circumstances may require separate analysis.
